title: if Statements and Basic Conditions
learningObjectives: Explain if statements and basic conditions in C++ decision logic.
Identify the condition and the branch paths it controls.
Trace execution for normal, boundary and unexpected values.
Write clear and correct decision statements for a practical case.
Review common mistakes such as ordering, nesting or missing fallback handling.

understand.concept: The if statement executes a block only when its condition evaluates to true. Conditions commonly use comparisons and Boolean expressions. A block is formed with braces to make the controlled statements clear.
understand.whyItMatters: Decision logic controls program behavior. Correct conditions, branch order, fallback paths and validation keep programs predictable and robust.
understand.explain: Use the examples to trace if statements and basic conditions; identify which branch is reached for each test input and explain why other branches are skipped.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five if statements and basic conditions examples. For each, record the condition outcome and executed branch. Change one input to test an alternate path.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ decision-based program applying if statements and basic conditions to a realistic scenario. Test at least three normal cases, two boundary cases and one invalid/unexpected case.
hints: Write the condition in plain language before coding.
Trace the branch that runs for each sample value.
Keep nesting shallow and branches explicit.
Include a fallback or validation path when appropriate.
